restaurant_name: de Welcome Massage เดอเวลคัมมาสสาจ
text:
⚠️ DISHONEST SHOP. Would NOT recommend 请避雷 ⚠️

We were a group of 5 deciding between several massage shops in Nimman when a male staff member approached us and convinced us to visit their other branch. The sign outside advertised a 1-hour foot massage for 300 THB, but after arriving we were told it was actually 350 THB as promotion ended.

He promised female therapists and complimentary coconut water, which influenced our decision to choose this shop. However, after 3 of us had already started washing our feet and preparing for the massage, we were suddenly asked whether we would accept male therapists because there were not enough female therapists available. The assurance that all 5 of us could receive massage together with female therapists was one of the main reasons we chose this shop. As a result, 2 of our friends left and went to other shops.

After the massage, we asked about the promised coconut water and were told it was only available if we left a review — a condition that was never mentioned beforehand. When we questioned this, the receptionist became defensive and claimed she would check the CCTV footage, but no footage was ever shown. She then called over the same male staff member, who changed his story and claimed he had informed us from the beginning, which was simply not true.

The massage itself was so mediocre and certainly not worth being pressured into leaving a review for a complimentary drink.

This review is not about coconut water. It is about misleading promises, inconsistent information, and the way customers are treated when they raise legitimate concerns.

This was one of the most disappointing service experiences we had in Chiang Mai. Would NOT recommend this shop and would strongly suggest that tourists look elsewhere, where there are plenty of massage shops nearby.

restaurant_name: de Welcome Massage เดอเวลคัมมาสสาจ
text:
My hairstylist strongly recommended this place, mentioning that the owner speaks Chinese.

Unfortunately, I visited on the afternoon of April 4th. When I entered, three staff members were serving customers.

No one greeted me or offered assistance. After looking around at the counter for a while, someone came over and asked me if this was the place, because the experience was so different from the Google reviews. Before paying, I even showed the staff a Google Map and asked if this was the place 😂 (The staff said yes!).

Then, the staff asked me to pay with a local mobile payment system, so I asked if I could pay in cash. (I rarely see foreigners using local payment systems.)

Then, a very pretty young lady appeared and led me to the third floor for a massage.

My misfortune began.

My clothes were missing a button, but since we're both women, I didn't mind too much. I chose the Hot Press + Thai Massage, thinking it would be a herbal ball massage, but it turned out to be a warm oil massage. All of this was still funny, but after the pretty young lady started massaging me for 10 minutes, I knew I was doomed…

Wouldn't it be impolite to ask for a different masseuse? 😵‍💫
Is it possible to change from 90 minutes to 60 minutes? But I already paid downstairs…😵‍💫
Is it because the masseuse is too thin that it hurts so much? 😵‍💫
Or is it because she's pressing on the right spots that it hurts so much? Should I ask her to be gentler? 😵‍💫
If I just say "stop, stop!" am I wasting my money? 😵‍💫

It's not just that she's so thin she has no muscle, only bones putting pressure on her. You can immediately tell from her movements that she has a standard operating procedure (SOP) in mind, but she's just going through the motions. She's not actually targeting the client's muscles or applying pressure. You can clearly see that what she's doing is just a fake movement; there might be pain, but she's not really stretching. And many of her poses are just empty gestures?

A soulless Thai massage left me feeling utterly exhausted, both physically and mentally. 😂😂😂 I even wondered if massage therapists have trainees?

But being a greedy little guy, I still finished. The masseuse knew I needed to use the restroom before going downstairs, so she packed up her tools and went down. When I slowly tidied myself up and went downstairs, I didn't see her. There were still three older women downstairs. I told them I was done, but no one paid any attention to me—no water, no hot tea, no greetings. I asked, "I'm finished, is that all?"

Nobody paid any attention to me. 🫤 I had no choice but to go outside, change my shoes, and leave.

I was very thirsty then; I should have at least asked for a glass of warm water.

When I got home, I had bruises on my abdomen, and both sides of my buttocks were extremely sore. I couldn't sleep well that night because of the body aches.

The next day, I was so uncomfortable I couldn't eat. While traveling by car, I had to keep changing positions because of the pain in my buttocks. I was genuinely surprised by how terrible this experience was 😵‍💫😵‍💫

All I can say is that after the massage, my whole body felt awful.

Next time, if it starts like this, I'll run away immediately and won't blindly trust Google reviews anymore 😭
